title: ～予定だ — plan to ～, be scheduled to ～
summary: Talks about plans and schedules that are already arranged: “I plan to ～ / it is scheduled to ～.” It attaches to the dictionary form of a verb or to a noun + の. It is used for trips, appointments and events.

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形 ＋ 予定だ／予定です
patterns.gloss: dictionary form + 予定だ (帰る予定です)

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ の ＋ 予定だ
patterns.gloss: noun + の + 予定: 来週の予定 (next week's schedule)

body.p: 予定 is for something decided, not just hoped for. 来月帰る予定です says that your return next month is already planned. A time expression is usually included. It can also describe other people and things: 会議は三時に始まる予定だ.
～つもりだ expresses the speaker's own intention. ～予定だ stresses an arrangement or schedule, which may involve other people, so it is the natural choice for timetables and business plans.

examples.ja: 来月（らいげつ）国（くに）へ帰（かえ）る予定（よてい）です。
examples.romaji: Raigetsu kuni e kaeru yotei desu.
examples.tr: I plan to return to my country next month.

examples.ja: 明日（あした）の午後（ごご）、友達（ともだち）と会（あ）う予定（よてい）です。
examples.romaji: Ashita no gogo, tomodachi to au yotei desu.
examples.tr: I'm scheduled to meet my friend tomorrow afternoon.

examples.ja: その会議（かいぎ）は三時（さんじ）に始（はじ）まる予定（よてい）だ。
examples.romaji: Sono kaigi wa sanji ni hajimaru yotei da.
examples.tr: That meeting is scheduled to start at three o'clock.

pitfalls: Use the dictionary form: 帰る予定, not 帰った予定 or 帰ている予定.
Do not use it for vague wishes. For something not yet decided, use ～たい or ～と思う.
